subject: Materials Science
title: Poisson's Ratio: Squeeze and Bulge
description: A quick, practical guide to Poisson's Ratio: Squeeze and Bulge.

hook.text: Stretch a rubber band and it gets thinner. Compress a ball and it bulges sideways. Same physics.

buildup.text: Poisson's ratio (ν) is the ratio of lateral strain to axial strain — typically 0.25 to 0.35 for metals.

discovery.text: It tells you how much a material contracts sideways when stretched — volume isn't quite conserved.

twist.text: Auxetic materials have negative Poisson's ratio — they get fatter when stretched. Foams can do this.

climax.text: Rubber has ν ≈ 0.5, meaning volume is nearly constant — it's essentially incompressible.

punchline.text: Pull in one direction and something always happens in the other.

quiz.question: What does Poisson's ratio describe?
options: How much a material heats up under stress
The ratio of lateral contraction to axial extension under load
The maximum stress a material can sustain
